component.name: Daint
component.summary: A simple, fast paint program for quick doodles

description.p: Daint is a deliberately simple raster paint program for when you just want to pull up a canvas and doodle, without the weight of GIMP or the fiddliness of a full image editor.

It has the tools you expect and a few that are just fun: pencil, eraser, spray, line, rectangle, ellipse, free-form polygon, flood fill, colour picker, and text, plus a rainbow brush that cycles the spectrum as you draw. A two-colour system (left and right mouse buttons), an editable colour palette, and crisp pixels by default with an optional smooth-edges mode. It opens PNG, JPEG, and BMP images, and saves to PNG.

For pixel-level work there is cursor-anchored zoom, an optional grid with a configurable cell size, rulers along the top and left edges, and a live coordinate readout. The canvas is resizable, and undo/redo covers your mistakes.

description.p: Adds an indexed-palette mode for editing sprites. Opening a palette-indexed PNG keeps it on its palette instead of converting to RGB, so it can be saved back without changing the colour table or its order. The colour controls are replaced by the image's own palette while editing, and a grid-size suggestion helps line the grid up with a sprite's tiles or frames.
The flood fill now matches colours exactly when smoothing is off, so it no longer spreads across similar shades, and the open and save dialogs remember the last folder used.
First release: pencil, eraser, line, rectangle, ellipse, flood fill, colour picker, palette, brush size, undo/redo, and image open/save (opens PNG/JPEG/BMP, saves PNG).
